definition: A branch of optimization dealing with problems where the objective function is convex, guaranteeing that any local minimum is also the global minimum.
details: While classical convex optimization theory provides strong guarantees, most deep learning loss functions are non-convex, meaning many of the guarantees from convex optimization theory don't directly apply, motivating more empirical and heuristic approaches to training.

explainer.lead: Convex optimization studies a particularly well-behaved kind of optimization problem, where finding a local minimum is enough to know you have found the best possible solution. Its guarantees are valuable, but they generally do not carry over to the non-convex loss functions used in deep learning.

tiers.eli5: A convex problem is like a single-bottomed bowl: however you roll the ball, it settles at the one lowest point. Many real problems are bumpier than that.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers reach for convex formulations when they need guaranteed convergence, but deep learning loss surfaces are non-convex, motivating more empirical and heuristic training approaches. A pitfall is assuming a local minimum is global.
tiers.paperLevel: A branch of optimization dealing with problems where the objective function is convex, guaranteeing that any local minimum is also the global minimum. This guarantee does not hold for non-convex objectives.

explainer.example: Minimize f(x) = (x - 3)^2 over real-valued x. This objective is convex, and its minimum occurs at x = 3, where f(3) = 0; because 0 is the smallest value a square can take, this local minimum is the global minimum.
explainer.intuition: A convex objective has no separate local dips that can be mistaken for the best overall solution. This makes the search for a minimum much more dependable than it is for a general non-convex objective.
howItWorks: Define the objective function whose value you want to minimize.
Establish that the objective is convex.
Optimize until you reach a local minimum.
Conclude that this point is also a global minimum.
explainer.whyItMatters: Convexity turns a local optimality result into a global one, providing a strong guarantee about solution quality. The contrast with non-convex deep learning losses also explains why training neural networks often relies on empirical and heuristic methods.
misconceptions: A local minimum of every optimization problem is globally optimal: the guarantee requires a convex objective.
Convex optimization guarantees that deep learning training finds the global minimum: most deep learning losses are non-convex.
